channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Kin Fai Mak, Xiaomeng Liu

Authors: Jinghao Deng, Jiabin Xie, Hongyuan Li, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Unconventional superconductivity and orbital magnetism in correlated graphene.

Tags: #superconductivity #graphene #correlatedelectrons #magnetism

Abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

item.title: [6] Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Fabio Caruso, Manfred Fiebig

Authors: Jan Gerrit Horstmann, Christoph Emeis, Andrin Caviezel, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Phonon control in WTe2, a material adjacent to user's telluride interest.

Tags: #phonon #ferroelectric #WTe2 #materialsscience

Abstract: Strong photoexcitation of phonons in a crystal can lead to a nonlinear response. Now it is shown that this breakdown of linearity can be overcome by the application of well-timed photoexcitation pulses in WTe2.

item.title: [8] Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. J. Millis, F. Boschini

Authors: D. Armanno, O. Gingras, F. Goto, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Time-resolved photoemission study of pseudogap and superconductivity in cuprates.

Tags: #photoemission #ARPES #cuprates #unconventionalsuperconductivity #pseudogap

Abstract: How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

item.title: [8] Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: K. Jin, N. E. Hussey

Authors: C. M. Duffy, S. J. Tu, Q. H. Chen, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: STS evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates.

Tags: #STM/STS #cuprates #unconventionalsuperconductivity #spinfluctuations

Abstract: The mechanism for superconductivity in cuprates is still not known. Now, the observation of a relationship between the critical temperature and strength of coupling between electrons and spin fluctuations suggests the latter as a prime candidate.
